title: wsblast run report (schema 1.x)
description: Output of `wsblast --format json` (also written by `-o FILE`). Derived from `JsonReport` in src/report.rs, `AggregatedMetrics` and `LatencyStats` in src/metrics.rs, and `ErrorCategory` in src/error.rs. Readers must ignore properties they do not know: fields may be added within schema 1.x without changing the major version.

schema_version.description: Report schema version. wsblast 0.1.x and 0.2.0 write "1.0.0".

target_url.description: Target URL after parsing, so a bare host gains a trailing slash (ws://127.0.0.1:9001 is written as ws://127.0.0.1:9001/). For a scenario this is the URL of the first phase that ran (or of the --phase phase); phase_targets lists every phase.

connections.description: Configured connection count (-c). For a scenario, the sum of every executed phase's connections, which equals metrics.total_connections_attempted.

duration_secs.description: Measured elapsed time in seconds (metrics.elapsed as a float), not the configured --duration. For a scenario, the sum of each phase's elapsed time; the 500 ms pause between phases is not included. For a distributed run (metrics.distributed present), the coordinator's time from sending start to receiving the last agent result.

mode.description: Session mode, printed with Rust Debug formatting.

phase_targets.description: Scenario runs only: the target of every executed phase, in run order. A phase skipped by Ctrl+C or SIGTERM is not listed. Absent from single-run reports and from reports written before it was added; readers should treat a missing value as an empty list.

phase.description: Phase name from the scenario file.

target_url.description: Target URL the phase connected to, after parsing (same format as target_url).

phases.description: Scenario runs only: every executed phase with its own metrics and SLO result, in run order. A phase skipped by Ctrl+C or SIGTERM is not listed. Absent from single-run reports and from reports written before it was added; readers should treat a missing value as an empty list. The counters of the phases add up to those of metrics.

duration.description: A Rust std::time::Duration as serialized by serde.

latency_stats.description: Summary of an HDR histogram with 1 us to 60 s bounds and 3 significant figures. All values are microseconds. Percentiles and max are the upper edge of the bucket that holds the value, so they can exceed the true sample by up to 0.1 %. When count is 0 every field is 0.

interval_latency.description: Latency percentiles of one time series interval, at 1% precision. Every field is 0 when no reply arrived in the interval.

time_series_point.description: Counters and latency of one interval. Latency is placed in the interval in which the reply arrived.

start_secs.description: Start of the interval, in seconds since the run started.

duration_secs.description: Length of the interval in seconds. Only the last interval of a run or scenario phase can differ from interval_secs.

active_connections.description: Connections open at the end of the interval.

throughput_msg_per_sec.description: The larger of messages_sent and messages_recv, per second of the interval.

time_series.description: The run broken down by time. The counters of all points add up to the run's totals.

interval_secs.description: Length of each interval in seconds: 1 for runs up to 600 seconds, otherwise the whole number of seconds that keeps a run within 600 points.

latency_basis.description: The latency each point reports: response_time for paced echo runs, rtt otherwise, mixed for a scenario whose phases differ. Empty when the run kept no series.

aggregated_metrics.description: Merged result of every worker. See METHODOLOGY.md for how each value is measured.

total_connections_attempted.description: Worker slots the run was configured to open (the -c value, or the sum over scenario phases). Slots that were never started because the run ended first are included.

total_connections_established.description: Worker slots that completed at least one handshake. Never larger than total_connections_attempted.

total_connections_failed.description: Started worker slots that never completed a handshake and recorded a connection error. total_connections_attempted equals total_connections_established + total_connections_failed + total_connections_interrupted + total_connections_not_started.

total_connections_interrupted.description: Started worker slots whose first handshake was still in progress when the run ended, so they neither succeeded nor failed and have no error recorded. Absent from reports written before this field was added; readers should treat a missing value as 0.

total_connections_not_started.description: Worker slots the ramp had not reached when the run ended, so they never tried to connect and have no error recorded. Absent from reports written before this field was added; readers should treat a missing value as 0.

total_reconnects.description: Handshakes that re-established a slot after its connection was lost. handshake_latency.count equals total_connections_established + total_reconnects. Absent from reports written before reconnects were added; readers should treat a missing value as 0.

total_messages_sent.description: Data frames written successfully. Keepalive pings, pongs and Close frames are not counted.

total_messages_recv.description: Data frames counted as received. In echo mode, replies recorded within the test window; in stream and listen mode, every text or binary frame read; in graphql-ws mode, next/data messages.

total_bytes_sent.description: Payload bytes of the counted sent frames. WebSocket framing, TLS and the HTTP upgrade are not included.

total_bytes_recv.description: Payload bytes of the counted received frames.

elapsed.description: Wall-clock time from the start of the run (before the first connection is spawned) to cancellation.

error_rate.description: Failed operations divided by attempted operations: errors / (total_messages_sent + errors that happened before a message was sent), where errors is the sum of error_breakdown. An error that ends an already-sent message (an echo reply timeout, a read error or a close while the reply is awaited) is counted as a failure but not as a second attempt. 0 when no operation was attempted. See METHODOLOGY.md section 6.

handshake_latency.description: Time from starting the connect (DNS, TCP, TLS and HTTP upgrade) to a completed WebSocket handshake. One sample per successful handshake, reconnects included.

message_rtt.description: Request to reply round-trip time, from the actual send to the reply. Only echo mode records samples; in every other mode count is 0.

response_time.description: Echo response time, from each request's scheduled send time to its reply, so it includes the time a request waited behind a slow reply (coordinated omission correction). Recorded only for paced echo runs (--rate); count is 0 otherwise. Absent from reports written before this field was added; readers should treat a missing value as an empty distribution.

time_series.description: The run broken down by time. Absent from reports written before this field was added.

capture.description: Totals of the --capture file. Present only when the run captured; absent from other reports and from reports written before this field was added. See METHODOLOGY.md section 11.

frames_written.description: Records written after the header line: text, binary and Close frames and connection open events.

frames_dropped.description: Records not written because the limit was reached, the writer queue was full or a write failed. frames_written + frames_dropped is every record the run produced.

distributed.description: Distributed runs (--agents) only: which agents generated the load. Absent from single-machine reports and from reports written before this field was added. The metrics are merged from the agents that sent their result; see METHODOLOGY.md section 12.

agents.description: Every agent of the run, as given to --agents, in that order.

lost_agents.description: Agents that disconnected or missed their result deadline after the run started, in --agents order. Their connections and messages are not in the report. Empty when every agent reported.

error_breakdown.description: Error count per category. Categories with no errors are omitted, so the object is empty on a clean run. Every failed handshake attempt, including failed reconnect attempts, adds one error.

name.description: Phase name from the scenario file.

target_url.description: Target URL the phase connected to, after parsing (same format as target_url).

metrics.description: Metrics merged from this phase's workers only. elapsed is the phase's own run time and the time series starts at the phase start (time 0).

slo.description: The phase's own slo: thresholds checked on its metrics, with check names that are not prefixed. Passes with no checks when the phase sets no SLO. The same checks appear in the top-level slo with the phase name prefixed.

name.description: Check name. Current values: "Latency p50", "Latency p95", "Latency p99", "Latency p99.9" ("Response time p50" and so on when the run recorded response time), "Error Rate", "Throughput (msg/s)". In the top-level slo of a scenario report, a check of a phase's own SLO is prefixed with the phase name and a colon, as in "spike: Latency p99".

target.description: Human-readable threshold, for example "<= 25ms", "<= 1.00%" or ">= 100.0". Not intended for parsing.

actual.description: Human-readable measured value, for example "219µs", "0.00%" or "74250.3". A latency check with no RTT samples reads "no RTT samples" and fails.

passed.description: True when every check passed, including when no SLO was set (checks is then empty). In the top-level slo, when false the process exits with code 2.

checks.description: One entry per configured threshold, in the order p50, p95, p99, p99.9, error rate, throughput. In the top-level slo of a scenario report, the checks of the whole run (the scenario's slo: mapping and the SLO flags) come first, followed by each phase's own checks in run order.
